world_behind.title: The children in the tents
world_behind.text: Benjamin's address is the founding covenant document of this people, and it created a nation that took a name upon itself. The children in the tents were little at the time. The record's first explanation of their unbelief is that they could not understand the words.

world_behind.title: The first disciplinary case in the church's history
world_behind.text: Verse 10 says plainly that nothing like it had happened before. There is no procedure, no precedent, and nothing written down to consult. What the chapter records is the making of a rule.

world_behind.title: A king declining jurisdiction
world_behind.text: Mosiah is handed a set of accused and says he will not judge them. He delivers them back into Alma's hands. The record makes no argument about separating powers; it shows a monarch refusing one, three chapters before he ends the monarchy.

world_behind.title: The escalation path, shown once
world_behind.text: Verse 7 sets out the chain: teachers deliver the accused to the priests, the priests bring them to Alma, who is the high priest. Three offices and two handoffs, set out in the space of one sentence, and the machinery is already running before anyone knows what to do at the end of it.

world_behind.title: Discipline administered as a roll
world_behind.text: The entire penalty is being numbered or not numbered among the people of the church, with names blotted out. There is no fine, no confinement, and no exile. The consequence is a list, and the phrase for it recurs three more times in this record, always in a church setting.

world_behind.title: Growth by dissension
world_behind.text: The unbelievers began as less than half the church and became more numerous, and verse 5 names the cause as dissensions among the brethren. The group grew because the other group argued.

words.text: What is handed down, in the neutral sense of received teaching rather than empty custom. The verse says they did not believe the tradition of their fathers, which places the content and the transmission together. What they rejected was something delivered rather than something demonstrated.

Warned and corrected, with the correction aimed at improvement rather than punishment. The verse makes it the church's own act on its own members. It appears again at verse 39, where the leaders are admonished in turn, which keeps the traffic running both ways.

Disturbed, unsettled in mind. It is used twice of Alma in four verses: troubled in his spirit when the case arrives, and troubled again when the king hands it back. The record tracks his distress, and the second occurrence is what sends him to prayer.

A trumpet, and by extension the signal it gives. The verse specifies the second one, distinguishing this rising from another the reader is expected to know about. The chapter does not explain the sequence; it assumes it.

Offenses against another party, carrying a sense of crossing a boundary rather than of general wrongdoing. The word runs three times through two verses, twice of offenses against God and once of offenses between neighbors, and the verses treat them as the same kind of debt.

Looking around carefully, watchfully. It describes how the church walked once the affairs were regulated, and Paul uses the same figure in writing to Ephesus. The image is of a people who can see what is around them. That is what the chapter's whole procedure is for.

phrases.term: They were a separate people as to their faith, and remained so ever after
phrases.text: A permanent division reported without comment, and the phrase occurs once in scripture. The clause "remained so ever after" reaches past the chapter and past the book. What began as children who could not follow a speech becomes a standing feature of the society.

Four words from a king, and they occur once in scripture. He is not declining out of modesty or difficulty; he simply says the case is not his and hands it back. Everything the chapter then produces exists because a monarch would not use the authority he had.

phrases.term: After he had poured out his whole soul to God
phrases.text: The chapter's turning point, and it occurs once in scripture. Two chapters earlier Alma's people had poured out their hearts under a ban on praying aloud. The same verb returns here for a leader with nobody forbidding him anything, and the result is a voice.

phrases.term: Thy exceeding faith in the words alone of my servant Abinadi
phrases.text: The Lord's account of what Alma had to work with in Noah's court: no sign, no angel, no corroborating witness, and a speaker already under sentence of death. The blessing is pronounced on the believing itself rather than on anything that came of it, and it arrives decades after the fact.

phrases.term: He that will hear my voice shall be my sheep
phrases.text: The membership test, given as a condition. John's Gospel has the same figure with the sheep hearing and the shepherd knowing. Here it is turned into an administrative instruction: him shall ye receive into the church, and him will I also receive.

phrases.term: As often as my people repent will I forgive them
phrases.text: A promise with no ceiling on it, and the clause occurs once in scripture. The verse immediately following requires the same of them toward each other and attaches a penalty for refusing. The unlimited offer and the obligation arrive together.

phrases.term: He wrote them down that he might have them
phrases.text: A revelation turned into a working document in one clause. The stated purpose is practical: so that he might judge the people according to the commandments of God. What the chapter has produced is a text he can consult.

The whole penalty, stated as a clerical act. The phrase appears three more times in this record, all in later church settings, which makes this verse the source of a standing practice. Nothing else is done to the people concerned.

verses.label: v. 1–5
verses.title: The ones who were too young
verses.text: They could not understand Benjamin, did not believe the tradition, did not believe the resurrection or the coming of Christ, would not be baptized, and became a separate people permanently. Then the number: fewer than half the church at first, and growing because of dissensions inside it.

verses.label: v. 6–10
verses.title: A case with no precedent
verses.text: Flattering words draw church members into sin; teachers deliver them to priests; priests bring them to Alma. He does not know what to do, there are many witnesses, and nothing like it has ever happened. The chapter is careful to say the problem is procedural.

verses.label: v. 11–14
verses.title: Two men who will not judge alone
verses.text: Alma brings them to the king so the king can judge them by their crimes. The king says he judges them not and hands them back. Alma, troubled a second time, pours out his whole soul, and a voice answers.

verses.label: v. 15–20
verses.title: Blessings, and a chain of belief
verses.text: Blessed for faith in Abinadi's words alone; blessed for faith in Alma's words alone; blessed for establishing a church; blessed for asking. Each link in the chain believed a man speaking, with no sign attached, and the Lord names that as the thing being blessed.

verses.label: v. 21–28
verses.title: Who is received, and who is not
verses.text: Hearing the voice makes a person a sheep, and the church is told to receive whom the Lord receives. Then the other side: those who never knew him will come forth at the second trump, will know him then, and will hear that he never knew them.

verses.label: v. 29–33
verses.title: The rule, and the writing of it
verses.text: Judge according to the sins committed; forgive the one who confesses and repents; forgive as often as repentance comes; forgive one another or stand condemned. Then Alma writes it down so he can use it, and the record says the practice was observed from that time forward.

verses.label: v. 34–39
verses.title: Applied, and what followed
verses.text: Those who confessed were numbered, those who would not had their names blotted out, and the affairs of the church were regulated. Then peace, prosperity, many baptized, and the leaders suffering afflictions and persecution from those outside, admonishing and being admonished in turn.

chapter.title: Unbelief is diagnosed first as a hearing problem
chapter.text: The first thing said about this generation is that they were little children when Benjamin spoke and could not understand him. Hardness of heart appears at verse 3, after the gap in comprehension.

chapter.title: There is no procedure, and the chapter is the making of one
chapter.text: Alma does not know what to do; the record says nothing like it had happened before; the king refuses the case; the answer has to be asked for. What exists afterward is a rule that did not exist at verse 6.

chapter.title: A king declines to judge, three chapters before he abolishes kings
chapter.text: "Behold, I judge them not" appears once in scripture. The record makes no argument from it and does not connect it to what Mosiah does later, but the two acts are the same instinct twice.

chapter.title: "Words alone," twice, and it is the thing being blessed
chapter.text: Alma believed Abinadi on nothing but his words; Alma's people believed Alma on nothing but his. The Lord repeats the phrase in consecutive verses and it appears nowhere else in scripture. A church has been built out of two links of testimony with no sign in either.

chapter.title: Revelation becomes a written law inside one verse
chapter.text: The same man who copied out Abinadi's sermon while being hunted writes this down so he can judge by it. This record consistently treats hearing something and preserving it as one act.

chapter.title: The penalty is a list
chapter.text: Numbered or not numbered; names blotted out. Nothing is done to a person's body, property, or freedom. The phrase recurs three times later in this record, always in a church context, which makes verse 36 the origin of a practice.

chapter.title: Forgiveness is made unlimited and reciprocal in two verses
chapter.text: As often as my people repent, I will forgive; and he that forgiveth not his neighbor stands condemned. The ceiling is removed from the divine side and an obligation attached on the human side, in adjacent sentences.

chapter.title: The last clause is two apostolic instructions in sequence
chapter.text: Pray without ceasing, and give thanks in all things. Those are the substance of 1 Thessalonians 5:17 and 5:18. Adjacent verses there, adjacent here, and in the same order. The chapter closes on them without introduction.

applications.title: Check whether they heard it
applications.text: The record's first account of this generation's unbelief is that they had been too young to follow the speech. Before concluding that someone has rejected something, find out whether it ever reached them in a form they could take in.

applications.title: Say when you do not know
applications.text: Alma was the high priest and had no idea what to do. He said so by his actions: took it to the king, then took it to God. Not knowing is a starting position.

applications.title: Decline the authority that is not yours
applications.text: Mosiah had the power to judge and said the case was not his. Holding an office does not make every decision in reach your decision to make.

applications.title: Write down what you are given
applications.text: He recorded the answer so he could use it later and apply it consistently. An insight you cannot reproduce next month is not yet a practice.

applications.title: Make the standard reciprocal before you enforce it
applications.text: The unlimited forgiveness and the obligation to forgive arrive in the same breath. If you are administering a rule, check that it binds you the same way.

applications.title: Let the consequence be proportionate to the sphere
applications.text: The church's whole penalty was membership. Where you have authority over one part of someone's life, keep the consequence inside that part.

applications.title: Be admonished as well as admonishing
applications.text: The leaders corrected their brethren and were corrected themselves, every one according to his own sins. Correction that only travels downward is not the practice described here.

questions.text: What did I dismiss before I actually understood it?
What am I handling badly because I have never admitted I do not know how?
What judgment have I made that was not mine to make?
Whose words alone have I believed, and was I right to?
Whom have I forgiven once and not twice?
Who is allowed to admonish me?
